page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton family processors. Built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 32 dedicated physical cores across 32 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. It provides 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache.

Hardware connectivity includes a baseline network throughput of 100 Gbps, tailored for network-intensive and clustered environments. The instance carries zero local storage, requiring network-attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent storage operations. It includes dedicated hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions, but omits graphics processing units or specialized vector accelerators like AVX-512 and AMX.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded and memory throughput capabilities. The instance achieved 21484.0 in Geekbench multi-core testing and reached 412.91 GB/sec in uncached read and 198.33 GB/sec in uncached write memory bandwidth. Database execution performance is high, scoring 47617.22 in PassMark database operations and processing 66.38 million Redis SET operations per second. In software compilation with Clang and static web serving, it demonstrated strong throughput at 71.82 GB/sec. Conversely, single-threaded processing and small-model token generation reflect moderate performance profiles.

The m8gn.8xlarge offers high computational density and memory bandwidth efficiency for ARM-optimized distributed applications, container fleets, caching clusters, and relational or key-value database engines operating over high-speed networks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.8xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton processor platform. Delivering 32 dedicated physical cores at 2.8 GHz alongside 128.0 GB of memory, it maintains a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Outfitted with a 100 Gbps baseline network interface and managed by the Nitro hypervisor, the server provides high network bandwidth but does not bundle local storage or GPUs, relying instead on network-attached EBS volumes. Benchmark testing demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute in Geekbench, exceptional memory read and write speeds, and strong database transaction execution, reaching 66.38 million Redis SET operations per second. It is well matched for high-throughput distributed architectures, memory caching clusters, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional database workloads.
